findings.title: Moving the retirement check ahead of the nextUsageDueAt/backoff returns removes the only throttle on handleAccountDead's failure retry, turning a no-target retirement into a 60-second full candidate sweep forever
findings.detail:
Two plan clauses combine into an unbounded loop.

(a) Line 27 requires the retirement check to run before the `nextUsageDueAt` / `backoff` early returns. (b) Line 40 reuses `handleAccountDead`'s "失败/no-target 路径" and only its "成功去重" — the early-exit in handleAccountDead (quota-monitor.ts:1364-1372) fires only when `existing.switchOutcome === "switched"`. A `no_account` / `switch_failed` outcome is re-entered on the very next pass.

Today the only thing that rate-limits that re-entry is `state.nextUsageDueAt`: the `local_scan` return at quota-monitor.ts:1645-1657 short-circuits every pass until usage is due (basePollMinutes=20, quota-monitor-config.ts:23). The existing test proves this is the load-bearing gate — it has to force `h.deps.state = { ...first.state, nextUsageDueAt: NOW }` to make the second attempt happen at all (src/__tests__/quota-monitor.test.ts:895-935). Pass cadence is `min(nextUsageDueAt, nextPaneScanDueAt, confirmDueAt)` (quota-monitor-cli.ts:98-106) and `nextPaneScanDueAt` advances by paneScanSeconds=60, so the daemon wakes every ~60s regardless.

So while the active account is retired and the switch cannot complete, every ~60s pass would run:
- `verifyAndRankCandidates` in full (handleAccountDead:1376-1381) — per candidate: a locked `readSnapshot` witness, `verifyCandidate` freshness probe, `readPoolCredential`, a live `fetchUsage` call, and a `recordObservation` → `recordObservationInStore` → `writeStore` disk write (account-store.ts:726-762). Note `verifyAndRankCandidates` gates on *live* usage, not on `quotaExhaustedUntil`, so quota-exhausted candidates are fetched every time before being excluded.
- `switchAccount` with `markUnavailable`, whose mark carries `markedAt: new Date(now).toISOString()` (quota-monitor.ts:1423-1432). `markAccountUnavailable` only no-ops on a byte-identical mark (account-store.ts:283-285), so `markedAt` differs every pass → `deadMarkNeedsWrite` is true → the store is rewritten on the no_account path every pass (switch-executor.ts:1030-1033), and the retired account's quarantine timestamp is continuously overwritten to "now", destroying the record of when retirement actually took effect.

That is a ~20x amplification over today's cadence: for a 5-account pool, ~5,760 usage-API calls and ~5,760 locked store writes per day instead of ~288. The failure mode is self-reinforcing: once the usage API rate-limits, every candidate is excluded as `unverifiable` (account-candidate-selector.ts:243-250) so `ranked` is permanently empty and no target can ever be found — and line 27 explicitly places the retirement check *before* `backoffUntilMs`, which is the one mechanism that would absorb rate limiting. There is also no `minSwitchIntervalMinutes` gate on this path (that check lives at quota-monitor.ts:1884-1890, only on the quota/model path after the usage read).

Failure scenario: business retires 2026-09-14T00:00:00-07:00 while active; school/personal/shopping are all over their 7d cap. Pass at 00:00 → handleAccountDead → 4 freshness probes + 4 usage fetches + 4 store writes → all excluded as quota → no_account → blocked episode. Pass at 00:01 → identical. By 02:00 the usage API is returning rate_limited, every candidate becomes `unverifiable`, and the pool never recovers even after school's reset — while the founder sees one `quota_no_target` alert and a quarantine `markedAt` that keeps ticking forward.

The plan needs an explicit throttle for the retirement path (e.g. a persisted retirement retry deadline alongside `deadAccountEpisode`, or reuse of `candidateSweepMinutes`), and a test asserting that two consecutive passes 60s apart do not re-run the candidate sweep. Line 28's "无候选保留既有 no-target 行为" does not cover this, because the *existing* no-target behavior includes the nextUsageDueAt gate the plan is removing.

findings.title: The pinned insertion point does not exist where the plan implies; satisfying it adds a locked readSnapshot + authority evaluation to every pass with undefined behavior on unresolved authority
findings.detail:
Line 27 says the retirement check must come after "取得可信 snapshot 并检查机器账号权威" but before the `nextUsageDueAt` early return. In pollOnce those are in the opposite order: the `nextUsageDueAt` → local_scan return is at quota-monitor.ts:1643-1657, and the locked `readSnapshot()` plus the `snapshot.authority.kind !== "resolved"` check are at 1672-1682. There is no trusted snapshot before the local_scan return — `deps.reconcileActive()` (1598) returns only a result/generation.

Satisfying the clause therefore requires a new `withAccountsLock(readSnapshot)` plus authority evaluation on every ~60s pass instead of every ~20min, and the plan does not say what an unresolved authority does on such a pass: alert + `finish("identity_conflict")` (which changes the outcome of every currently-local_scan pass and suppresses pane revive/confirmation work) or silently skip the retirement check and fall through. It also does not bound the added contention on the accounts lock, which switch-executor holds across fenced Keychain writes with a heartbeat.

Pin the exact insertion point and add tests for: (a) unresolved authority + usage not due still returns `local_scan`, (b) `activeCredential === null` / expired still reaches the retirement check, (c) `backoffUntilMs > now` still reaches it. R2 raised this as `retirement-check-placement-early-returns` and the R3 revision restated the intent without resolving the ordering.

findings.title: min-deadline selection plus the account_dead path (which bypasses minSwitchInterval) allows a multi-switch storm when several accounts retire close together
findings.detail:
Line 25 selects the "min-deadline 候选" and line 9 ranks by `min(resetMs, retiresAtMs)`, so the selector deliberately prefers the account closest to its own retirement. The retirement switch runs through `handleAccountDead`, which never reaches the anti-flap gate `now - state.lastSwitchAt < minSwitchIntervalMinutes * 60_000` (quota-monitor.ts:1884-1890) — that gate sits after the usage read on the quota/model path only.

Failure scenario: the founder cancels two subscriptions with the same billing date, so `business` retires at 00:00 and `personal` at 00:05. At 00:00 business retires; `personal` has the earliest min-key so it is ranked first and becomes active. At 00:05 personal retires and the system switches again. Each switch is a Keychain write, a runner-pane disruption, a terminal `unavailable` quarantine and an `account_dead`-routed founder notification — N switches within minutes, with nothing in the design placing a floor on it.

R2's `retirement-switch-vs-min-switch-interval` MEDIUM asked whether the retirement trigger is subject to the anti-flap gate; the R3 move to `account_dead` removes the gate entirely rather than answering. Either state a minimum remaining-life threshold for choosing a retiring candidate, or explicitly accept the storm and cover it with a test.

findings.title: "无效 retiresAt 只使该账户不可选" is a candidate-side rule with no defined meaning for the active account, and the validator's input domain is narrower than what the store can hold
findings.detail:
Lines 8 and 29 define invalid `retiresAt` as making the account 不可选 — a notion that only exists for switch *targets*. The R2 exception (line 25) makes the ACTIVE account's `retiresAt` load-bearing, and the plan never says what an invalid value there means: fail-open (keep running, feature silently off, no operator signal anywhere — the capacity/patrol surface would show a normal-looking account) or fail-closed (treat as retired → immediate forced switch + terminal quarantine). Both are defensible and they are opposite behaviors; per CLAUDE.md this is exactly the "confusion = stop" case rather than an implementer's judgment call.

This is also the most likely operator mistake in practice: line 32 has the Lead/QA hand-write the value into production `~/.flywheel/claude-accounts.json` and line 48 defers the lock-respecting setter to follow-ups.

Second, the validator's input domain is under-specified. `readStoreStrict` (account-store.ts:687-720) type-checks `name`, `quotaExhaustedUntil`, `weeklyResetAt`, `switchCooldownUntil` and `unavailable`, but would accept `retiresAt: 1789000000000`, `retiresAt: {}` or `retiresAt: []` unchanged. Item 1 lists only date-only / offset-less / invalid dates, so the shared helper must be specified to take `unknown` and reject non-strings, not just malformed date strings.

findings.title: The revive-window clamp names one epoch creation site; there are two
findings.detail:
Line 41 requires clamping "对来源账号设置了 retiresAt 的既有 revive 窗口" to the retirement instant, phrased as if there is a single window. `state.reviveEpoch` is created in two places:
- quota-monitor.ts:2179-2186 — account trigger, `expiresAt = Date.parse(accountTrigger.resetAt) + REVIVE_GRACE_MS`.
- quota-incident.ts:137-145 (`finalizeModelSwitch`) — model-cap trigger, `expiresAt = computeModelReviveExpiresAt(benchUntilByModel, finalizedAt)`.

Both carry `sourceAccount` and both feed `reviveScan`'s `authorized` gate (quota-revive-scan.ts:312-321). If only the account path is clamped, a model-cap switch away from an account that later retires leaves an epoch that keeps authorizing revive attempts against a retired source past its retirement — the precise state the ruling exists to forbid. Name both sites in the plan and require a test for each.

findings.title: Reusing account_dead forces a terminal `unavailable` quarantine that is persisted even when no switch target exists, and the repo has no command to clear it
findings.detail:
The R3 choice of `account_dead` is right on the fabrication grounds, but it carries a consequence the plan does not state. An `account_dead` switch is *rejected* without a `markUnavailable` for the observed profile (switch-executor.ts:771-781), and on the no-candidate path the mark is written anyway before returning `no_account` (switch-executor.ts:1030-1033) — so the retired account gets a terminal quarantine while it is still the active account.

`unavailable` is documented as "Terminal account exclusion. Only an explicit operator command removes it" (account-store.ts:88), but no such command exists anywhere in the repo — the only clear path is hand-editing `~/.flywheel/claude-accounts.json`. It survives `quota-pool-rebuild`, which resets `authExpired`/`refreshTokenInvalid`/`profileVerifyFailed` but not `unavailable` (quota-pool-rebuild.ts:1037-1050). It also permanently adds `structural: account_unavailable:<name>` to the capacity snapshot (capacity-snapshot.ts:396-402) and flips `authUnusable` for that account.

Combined with the hand-edited config (line 32) and the deferred setter (line 48): a wrong `retiresAt` — wrong year, or `-07:00` vs `-08:00` across the Nov DST boundary — forces an immediate switch and terminally quarantines a healthy paid account, and correcting `retiresAt` afterwards does not undo it. Either add a sanity bound before firing (refuse a `retiresAt` implausibly far in the past) or write the exact recovery procedure into the handoff so QA/Lead know the quarantine is not self-healing.

findings.title: "持久化的去重标记" admits two readings with very different rollback consequences; name the mechanism
findings.detail:
"成功/已入投递队列后不重复" maps onto lead-alert.sh's receipt table (`eventId = sha1(project|lead|kind|signature)`, `sent`/`queued_transient` receipts, scripts/lead-alert.sh:464-600), which is the correct choice. But the literal phrase "持久化的账号+到期时间去重标记" also reads as a new QuotaMonitorState field, and that route is known-bad: parseState enforces an exact key set (`hasOnlyKeys(value, V2_STATE_KEYS)`, quota-monitor-state.ts:1003), so a rolled-back binary rejects the file and falls through to `conservativeState`, discarding `alertOutbox`. R2 raised exactly this (`retirement-warning-state-schema-and-rollback`) and line 43 parked it without answering, leaving the ambiguity in the pinned text. Say "signature-based dedup via the existing alert receipt store; no QuotaMonitorState schema change" explicitly.

Minor efficiency note on the receipt route: at a 60s pass cadence the monitor would spawn lead-alert.sh ~60 times across the warning window, each shelling out to sqlite3 to answer "duplicate". A cheap in-pass check (warn only on the first pass that crosses into the window) avoids that without needing persistence.

findings.title: "现有告警面" does not name the alert kind, and the unknown-kind fallback contradicts "不发 founder 私信"
findings.detail: Routing is strictly per-kind (quota-monitor-alert.ts:58-93). An unrecognized kind falls back to `{ mention: true, severe: true }` (quota-monitor-alert.ts:221-225), which resolves a mention target from `FLYWHEEL_QUOTA_ALERT_MENTION_USER` / `FLYWHEEL_FOUNDER_USER_ID` and duplicates the alert into `FLYWHEEL_QUOTA_ALERT_SEVERE_CHANNEL_ID`. Naming the kind (and its ROUTING entry) is what makes "不发 founder 私信" and severity=warning testable rather than emergent.

findings.title: Keeping the headroom grouping means the soon-to-retire account is often the one that gets skipped — record it as a known limitation
findings.detail: Line 9 applies `min(resetMs, retiresAtMs)` inside the existing groups. An account with `fiveH.pct >= trigger5hPct` is pushed to `highFiveH` and is only used when `healthy` is empty (account-candidate-selector.ts:338-341), regardless of how soon it retires. So the account that most needs to be burned down before expiry is the one most likely to be passed over. This follows correctly from "保留 headroom 分组" and the Lead's single-formula ruling, but the founder's framing is "早于下次 reset 的号优先用光" — write the limitation into the handoff so the ranking is not read as a guarantee.

findings.title: 2026-09-14T00:00:00-07:00 retires business at the start of 9/14, discarding the quota the feature exists to burn
findings.detail: If the business subscription actually runs *through* 2026-09-14, retiring at 00:00 PT on 9/14 throws away the last full day of paid quota — the inverse of the stated goal. The plan already flags "具体业务时间须确认" (line 18) and calendar-ruling.md records that the Lead raised the ordering contradiction with the founder, so this is a handoff condition rather than a design defect: make the production config write (line 32) blocked on an explicit founder confirmation of the *instant*, not just the calendar date.

findings.title: Item 6 and the R3 paragraph state two different verification contracts
findings.detail: Line 13 commits to `pnpm lint`, `pnpm -r build` and `pnpm test:packages:run` on the host; line 43 says host scope is targeted tests + lint/build with the full suite left to exact-head CI. Both are in the pinned plan. Reconcile them so the handoff's "what was actually run" statement cannot be read as the superset — per MEMORY's repeated finding that a locally-green focused suite is not a CI-green head, the narrower claim has to be the one written down.
